claims.statement: For any finite poset with linear restrictions on additive fibers, the coboundary composition satisfies (d1 d0 s)(a,b,c) = K_{c,b,a}(s(c)) identically for every section s.
dependencies: Finite poset with comparable triples a <= b <= c.
Additive fiber spaces F(x) and linear restriction maps preserving subtraction.
Definitions of coboundary operators d0 and d1.
Definition of composition curvature operator K_{c,b,a} = r_{b,a} r_{c,b} - r_{c,a}.
claims.limits: Applies to linear restriction systems on finite posets; does not assert an infinity-categorical model structure or physical gauge curvature.

claims.statement: On any finite poset with linear restrictions, curvature K = 0 everywhere is equivalent to nilpotency d1 d0 = 0 on all sections and to chain composability r_{c,a} = r_{b,a} r_{c,b}.
dependencies: Coboundary-curvature identity AUDIT-N004-006: (d1 d0 s)(a,b,c) = K_{c,b,a}(s(c)).
Fiber inhabitation: for every v in F(c), existence of a section with s(c) = v.
Definition of Flat system and chain composability.
claims.limits: Established for linear restriction systems on finite posets with inhabited fibers.

claims.statement: On an elementary diamond with one-dimensional scalar fibers, restriction maps alpha, beta, and composite mu yield curvature K(v) = (beta * alpha - mu) * v.
dependencies: Elementary diamond poset a < b < c with 1D vector fibers.
Scalar representation of linear maps between 1D vector spaces.
Definition of curvature defect K = r_{b,a} r_{c,b} - r_{c,a}.
claims.limits: Specific to one-dimensional scalar fibers where multiplication is commutative and associative.

claims.statement: Exact rational squaring encloses the algebraic number 2(sqrt(2)-1) strictly between 828/1000 and 829/1000 with certified width 1/1000.
dependencies: Definition of the algebraic number q = 2(sqrt(2)-1).
Exact rational field arithmetic in Q.
Monotonicity of the squaring mapping t -> (1 + t/2)^2 on positive reals.
claims.limits: Algebraic rational enclosure for 2(sqrt(2)-1); does not certify arbitrary transcendental numbers or replace metric deficit procedures.
